projects.name: Trajectory Inference via AI-guided Cross-view Evidence (TRACE)
projects.description: I develop TRACE, an LLM-guided trajectory inference agent and end-to-end Python/LangGraph package for scRNA-seq, scATAC-seq, and spatial transcriptomics analysis.
highlights: Develop TRACE, an LLM-guided trajectory inference agent that achieves high agreement with reference trajectories across evaluated scRNA-seq, scATAC-seq, and spatial transcriptomics datasets while automatically identifying root states from molecular evidence.

Build trace, an end-to-end Python package using LangGraph to coordinate R/Seurat analysis and LLM reasoning. Use Seurat for normalization, dimensionality reduction, clustering, and marker-gene analysis, and Signac for scATAC-seq preprocessing and gene-activity estimation.
Design structured prompts and targeted molecular-evidence queries to integrate UMAP and t-SNE views for cell-type annotation, lineage reconstruction, and root identification.

Develop spatial trajectory inference combining molecular evidence and spatial neighborhood graphs to distinguish repeated local processes. Implement graph-based pseudotime estimation with local root cells, retaining ambiguous assignments and partially resolved trajectories.
Design pPOS to jointly evaluate lineage membership and within-lineage ordering. Implement blockwise pair counting and inclusion-exclusion to avoid double-counting cell pairs shared across branches.

Investigate discrepancies in dyneval-based F1branches evaluation. Reimplement the metric according to its published definition over the full cell set, with diagnostics for cell coverage and branch recovery.
Implement comparative evaluation of TRACE, Monocle 3, Slingshot, and TSCAN using branch membership and within-lineage pseudotime ordering.

projects.name: Med2State
projects.description: I develop Med2State, a Python/PyTorch deep learning model for structured patient-state representations from incomplete multimodal records and longitudinal clinical history.
highlights: Develop Med2State, a deep learning model in Python and PyTorch that learns structured patient-state representations from incomplete multimodal records and longitudinal clinical history, with separate disease, procedure, and treatment channels.
Build modular encoders for demographics, measurements, structured EHR events, text, and images. Explore semantic cross-attention, low-rank fusion, and temporal models for irregular visits.
Develop learning objectives and clinical concept readouts for incomplete longitudinal records.

projects.name: Visual LLM-Guided Spatial Domain Detection (L-STAR)
projects.description: I developed L-STAR, combining Python LLM workflows for spatial-domain method selection with consensus clustering in R and spatial expression analysis using Seurat and SpatialExperiment.
highlights: Developed L-STAR, an LLM-guided spatial domain detection framework that achieved the highest average normalized ARI across evaluation datasets, outperforming individual methods and fixed-method consensus.
Designed structured prompts and implemented Python workflows to compare candidate domain maps using tissue context and optional histology.
Implemented repeated pairwise comparisons and win-rate ranking for method selection. Combined selected domain assignments through co-assignment matrices and consensus clustering in R.

Processed spatial expression data with Seurat and SpatialExperiment and built marker-guided domain annotation. Distinguished tissue regions from cell types by sampling level, retaining Unknown for insufficient evidence. Evaluated agreement using BioLORD-2023 embeddings and within-dataset permutation tests.

Benchmarked L-STAR across six spatial transcriptomics datasets against individual methods and fixed-method consensus. Assessed sensitivity to ensemble size, LLM choice, color palettes, and presentation order, and quantified selected-method redundancy.

projects.name: PaperEval
projects.description: I built OpenReview data pipelines, fine-tuned acceptance-prediction and response-grading models, and used the fine-tuned grader to evaluate generated author responses.
highlights: Built resumable OpenReview pipelines using Selenium and asynchronous requests, with structured JSON storage for papers, reviews, scores, and responses. Extracted author contact information from PDFs with PyMuPDF to enrich submission metadata.
Prepared training data and fine-tuned GPT-4o for paper acceptance prediction. Evaluated predictions using progressively richer inputs comprising paper metadata, reviewer scores, and review text.
Developed LLM-based agents to assess figures and tables in the context of full manuscripts and suggest improvements to clarity, readability, and presentation.
Fine-tuned GPT-4o mini as an LLM-based grader to score and compare author responses. Constructed proxy scoring targets from acceptance levels using bounded Gaussian noise.
Trained a reply-generation model and used the fine-tuned grader to compare generated responses with author replies from accepted and rejected submissions.

projects.name: MUDAC (Midwest Undergraduate Data Analysis Competition) 2025
projects.description: I engineered mentoring-match features and modeled match duration and closure with survival analysis, a causal Bayesian network, and a mixture-of-experts model.
highlights: Engineered features from sparse, high-dimensional numerical and text data for mentoring-match prediction, including embeddings, sentiment scores, and pairwise similarities.
Modeled match duration and closure using Cox proportional hazards regression and a causal Bayesian network.
Designed a mixture-of-experts model with regression, MLP, and Transformer experts for different feature types and a learned gating network. Compared it with random forest and XGBoost baselines.
Placed 7th in Innovation & Creativity among approximately 200 undergraduate teams at MUDAC 2025.
projects.status: 7th in Innovation & Creativity among approximately 200 undergraduate teams

projects.name: UMN & Hennepin County Public Health Equity Data Challenge
projects.description: I investigated inequities in mental-health resource access and developed a prediction interface using Hennepin County questionnaire data.
highlights: Investigated inequities in access to mental-health resources using Hennepin County questionnaire data. Applied multiple regression, ridge regression, decision trees, and causal inference methods.
Developed a tkinter interface for mental-health prediction using AdaBoost in scikit-learn.
Co-authored the analysis report and poster and placed in the top 25% of the undergraduate division.

projects.name: Overlapping Group LASSO Regression R Package Implementation
projects.description: I compared overlapping group LASSO implementations through a simulation study and implemented the optimized algorithm in C for R integration.
highlights: Compared overlapping_LeastR from the MATLAB SLEP library with oglasso in the R package VennLasso under matched problem sizes and convergence tolerances.
Designed a simulation study with 1,000 large sparse-matrix datasets and overlapping groups. Compared implementation runtimes using t-tests.
Implemented the optimized overlapping-group LASSO algorithm in C for integration with R.

work.name: Department of Biostatistics and Bioinformatics, Duke University
highlights: Help develop and refine BIOSTAT 830, a new course first offered in Fall 2026 to bridge undergraduate statistical theory and PhD-level inference. Quickly adapt lecture materials and proof-based assignment solutions while building course resources from the ground up.

Hold weekly office hours and grade assignments for a class of 22 students in statistical inference, asymptotic theory, and decision theory. Discuss common errors with the instructor to guide future lectures.
Prepare and verify proof-based LaTeX solutions, format and proofread slides, and manage materials in Canvas. Standardize notation and convert formulas into editable PowerPoint equations.

Prepared instructional slides and managed course materials in Canvas for the teaching team. Held office hours and graded weekly assignments and exam responses through Gradescope.
